thread:
anya: Noticed weird duplicate token lines in invoice preview during the alias->fallback rollout. Repro on staging: client hit `rico-main` -> fallback to `rico-quant`, preview shows two separate token rows. Anyone tracking meter events?

devon: I saw it too. Root cause: proxy issues a new req_id for fallback. Metering downstream keys by req_id so fallback becomes a new independent event instead of an update to the original.

frank: Fun. Options: (A) emit canonical_id at ingress before fallback so downstream can dedupe, (B) aggregator-side microbatch coalescer that merges events with matching fingerprint within ~1s, (C) post-processing reconciliation that collapses duplicates before final invoice generation.

liam: Tradeoffs: A is deterministic but needs a schema bump and consumer opt-in. B avoids schema churn but adds aggregator CPU and complexity. C is easiest short-term but delays invoice finality and is confusing for customers.

ops-eng: For a fast canary I'd recommend B behind a feature flag: microbatch coalescer with bounded memory that merges by fingerprint=(tenant_id|session_id|prompt_hash_prefix) within a 750ms window. Keep it LRU-evicted and size-limited per-tenant to avoid OOM on hotspots.

anya: I like B for quick mitigation. Can we also sample canonical_id at edge so we can validate correctness end-to-end before we commit to schema changes?

devon: Yes. Plan: edge will emit canonical_request_id + canonical_model_alias when sampling flag is on (2% initially). Aggregator coalescer will run for canary traffic. We'll compare the merge decisions between fingerprinting and canonical_id matches.

liam: Consumer migration: add consumer config feature `use_canonical_id=false` default. Billing joins can flip tenant-by-tenant. We should also add a compatibility layer in the joiner that falls back to fingerprint join if canonical_id absent.

frank: Microbatch coalescer sketch:

- maintain small in-memory windowed map keyed by fingerprint
- each entry: earliest_event, total_tokens_accum, highest_confidence_model_tag
- on incoming event: if fingerprint found and now - earliest_event.ts < 750ms then merge else emit and start new entry
- periodically flush entries older than 750ms

Pros: minimal schema churn. Cons: adds small CPU/memory and a slight change in event ordering semantics.

ops-eng: We'll also add a fallback safe-guard: if the coalescer sees >50k merges/min or latency regresses, flip it off automatically. Add a circuit breaker metric `billing.coalescer_health` and auto-rollback.

anya: Console UX: mark previews as "Provisional (dedupe in progress during routing rollouts)" and show a tooltip with a short explanation and a link to KB. Also suppress preview email notifications for canary tenants.

console-ux: We'll add a small pill "Provisional" next to preview totals and a hover tooltip: "Preview values are provisional during routing rollouts and may include transient duplicate lines. Final invoice will reconcile duplicates." Will mock this up and drop screenshots in the ticket.

devon: Telemetry plan: emit metrics `billing.preview_dup_fraction` (fraction of tokens deduped in preview), `billing.coalescer_merges_per_min`, `billing.preview_settle_delta_tokens`. Alert rule: page if `billing.preview_dup_fraction > 0.3%` sustained 15m or `billing.coalescer_merges_per_min > 10k` for 5m.

frank: Reconciliation SQL for final invoice pass (different approach from previous run): use windowing to pick the most authoritative event per fingerprint when canonical_id missing:

WITH grouped AS (
  SELECT *, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY coalesce(canonical_request_id, fingerprint) ORDER BY event_ts ASC) as rn
  FROM meter_events WHERE event_ts BETWEEN :start AND :end
)
INSERT INTO invoice_lines (tenant_id, request_id, tokens, model_tag)
SELECT tenant_id, coalesce(canonical_request_id, fingerprint), sum(tokens), max(model_tag) FROM grouped WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY tenant_id, coalesce(canonical_request_id, fingerprint);

This collapses duplicates using canonical_id when present, otherwise fingerprint.

liam: Important: when accepting canonical_id we should preserve an audit trail: keep original raw meter events in cold storage so finance can audit per-request history if needed. Also add docs for finance explaining the dedupe logic.

ops-eng: Rollout steps: 
1) deploy aggregator coalescer behind FF to 2% traffic for 30m
2) enable edge sampling of canonical fields at 2% in parallel
3) compare matches between canonical_id and coalescer decisions, monitor `billing.preview_dup_fraction` and `billing.preview_settle_delta_tokens`
4) if metrics stable (<0.1%), expand coalescer to 25% -> 100% and start consumer opt-ins; if coalescer looks good, schedule full schema bump for canonical_id emission
5) enable reconciliation job for the transition window and run settlement pass nightly until fully migrated

billing-bot: Created ticket BILL-1102 to track: coalescer implementation, edge sampling PR, consumer config, KB update, and finance sync.

anya: Timeline: devon/frank will have a coalescer PR ready today for perf tests. Edge sampling PR tomorrow. liam will add consumer flag and fallbacks. console-ux will drop mockups by EOD. We'll reconvene after 2% canary results.

devon: PRs: aggregator coalescer draft https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/9991, edge sampling draft https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/9992. Deploy-bot: deploy ingest-edge v4.9.3 -> canary (2%) ✅

ops-eng: Added temporary alert suppression for preview-email automation for canary cohorts per BILL-1102.

anya: Thanks everyone. Tagging @billing-team @finance @console-ux. We'll avoid sending preview emails to customers in the affected canary until reconciliation verifies final numbers. :mag:
